[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-008-file-pattern-rule-authoring-guidance.md#purpose-statement]

### Purpose Statement

This guidance provides step-by-step instructions for authoring file-pattern rules — the context-sensitive behavioral directives that activate when an AI agent works on files matching a specific glob pattern. File-pattern rules are a specialized form of the Instruction construct category in the unified taxonomy ([ADR-TEC-020](../../../../decisions/technology/ADR-TEC-020-ai-coding-assistant-construct-taxonomy.md)). This guidance implements [STD-TEC-AI-005](../../../../standards/technology/ai-development/STD-TEC-AI-005-file-pattern-instruction.md) and covers when to use rules vs. Skills, glob pattern design, Claude Code rules (`.claude/rules/`) vs. GitHub Copilot instructions with `applyTo:`, and cross-tool equivalence.
page_texts.5:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-008-file-pattern-rule-authoring-guidance.md#business-value]

### Business Value

- **Precision** — Rules activate only when relevant files are involved, reducing noise in agent context
- **Lightweight governance** — Enforce standards on specific file types without full Skill overhead
- **Cross-vendor portability** — Rules map between Claude Code and GitHub Copilot with clear equivalence
- **Composability** — Rules layer on top of Skills without modifying Skill definitions
page_texts.6:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-008-file-pattern-rule-authoring-guidance.md#target-audience]

### Target Audience

- **Primary**: Developers authoring repository-level AI configurations
- **Secondary**: Platform engineers maintaining rule catalogs
- **Stakeholders**: Technology Domain EA Lead, AI coding assistant governance
page_texts.8:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-008-file-pattern-rule-authoring-guidance.md#applicable-scenarios]

#### Applicable Scenarios

- Enforcing coding standards on specific file types (e.g., "all `.py` files must use type hints")
- Adding context when agents work in specific directories (e.g., "files in `iac/` use Terraform")
- Preventing modifications to protected files (e.g., "never edit files in `.github/agents/`")
- Providing file-type-specific conventions without creating a full Skill

[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-008-file-pattern-rule-authoring-guidance.md#scope-boundaries]

#### Scope Boundaries

- **In Scope**: Rule file structure, glob patterns, decision criteria for rules vs. Skills, cross-vendor mapping
- **Out of Scope**: Skill authoring (see [STD-TEC-AI-001](../../../../standards/technology/ai-development/STD-TEC-AI-001-skill-authoring.md)); instruction file structure (see [STD-TEC-AI-003](../../../../standards/technology/ai-development/STD-TEC-AI-003-instruction-file.md))
page_texts.11:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-008-file-pattern-rule-authoring-guidance.md#business-context]

### Business Context

Rules provide a lightweight mechanism to inject file-specific constraints into AI agent behavior without the overhead of a full Skill definition. They are the most granular level of behavioral configuration — bridging the gap between broad instruction files and comprehensive Skills.
page_texts.12:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-008-file-pattern-rule-authoring-guidance.md#technical-context]

### Technical Context

File-pattern rules exist in different forms across AI coding assistants:

| Platform | Mechanism | Location | Activation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Claude Code | Rule files with `paths:` frontmatter | `.claude/rules/*.md` | When agent touches matching files |
| GitHub Copilot | Instructions with `applyTo:` patterns | `.github/instructions/*.instructions.md` | When matching files are in context |
page_texts.13:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-008-file-pattern-rule-authoring-guidance.md#taxonomy-relationship]

### Taxonomy Relationship

Per [ADR-TEC-020](../../../../decisions/technology/ADR-TEC-020-ai-coding-assistant-construct-taxonomy.md), rules are a specialized form of **Instruction** — behavioral context that shapes reasoning, scoped to specific file patterns rather than the entire repository.

[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-008-file-pattern-rule-authoring-guidance.md#naming-conventions]

### Naming Conventions

| Element | Convention | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Claude rule file | kebab-case, concern name + `.md` | `drawio.md`, `terraform.md`, `python-tests.md` |
| Copilot instruction file | kebab-case, concern name + `.instructions.md` | `drawio.instructions.md`, `terraform.instructions.md` |
| Location (Claude) | `.claude/rules/` | `.claude/rules/drawio.md` |
| Location (Copilot) | `.github/instructions/` | `.github/instructions/drawio.instructions.md` |
page_texts.16:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-008-file-pattern-rule-authoring-guidance.md#naming-decision-tree]

### Naming Decision Tree

```
Does the rule govern a single file type or tool?
├── Yes → Use the tool/format name: `drawio.md`, `terraform.md`, `mermaid.md`
└── No →
    Does it govern a directory or concern area?
    ├── Yes → Use the concern name: `iac.md`, `components.md`, `docs.md`
    └── No →
        Does it combine a language with a specialization?
        └── Yes → Use language-specialization: `python-tests.md`, `csharp-adapters.md`

Is the rule platform-specific (applies only to one vendor)?
├── Yes → Still create both files (keep in sync per PTN-TEC-AI-003)
└── No → Same content in both locations with vendor-native frontmatter
```

**Anti-patterns to avoid:**

- `rule1.md`, `misc.md` — no semantic meaning
- `DON'T_DO_THIS.md` — violates kebab-case, shouty
- `all-my-rules.md` — one concern per file; split by domain
- `rules-for-typescript-react-components-in-the-frontend.md` — too long; use `react-components.md`

[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-008-file-pattern-rule-authoring-guidance.md#glob-pattern-conventions]

### Glob Pattern Conventions

| Pattern | Matches | Use Case |
|---|---|---|
| `*.py` | All Python files in root | Rarely useful alone |
| `**/*.py` | All Python files recursively | Python coding standards |
| `iac/**/*.tf` | Terraform files under `iac/` | IaC conventions |
| `.github/agents/*.agent.md` | Agent definition files | Agent authoring rules |
| `docs/**/*.md` | All markdown in docs | Documentation standards |
| `**/test_*.py` | All Python test files | Testing conventions |
| `components/*/src/**` | All source in components | Component coding rules |
page_texts.20:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-008-file-pattern-rule-authoring-guidance.md#rule-content-guidelines]

### Rule Content Guidelines

1. **Be directive** — Use imperative language ("Always include", "Never modify", "Use type hints for").
2. **Be specific** — Rules should add value beyond what the Skill already provides.
3. **Be concise** — Rules should be 5–20 lines. If longer, consider a Skill instead.
4. **Reference standards** — Link to the enterprise standard being enforced.
5. **No workflow steps** — Rules are constraints, not procedures. Use Commands/Prompts for workflows.
page_texts.22:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-008-file-pattern-rule-authoring-guidance.md#decision-tree-rules-vs-skills]

### Decision Tree: Rules vs. Skills

```
Is this behavioral guidance for a specific file type or directory?
├── No → Use a Skill (domain expertise) or Instruction (repo-wide context)
└── Yes →
    Is it more than 20 lines of content?
    ├── Yes → Use a Skill — the content is complex enough to warrant full structure
    └── No →
        Does it define a multi-step workflow?
        ├── Yes → Use a Command/Prompt — workflows are not rules
        └── No →
            Is it a constraint, convention, or contextual hint?
            └── Yes → Use a Rule
```
page_texts.23:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-008-file-pattern-rule-authoring-guidance.md#when-rules-are-appropriate]

### When Rules Are Appropriate

| Appropriate | Not Appropriate |
|---|---|
| "Python files must use type hints" | "How to write a Python microservice" (Skill) |
| "Terraform files must use the standard backend" | "Deploy infrastructure to AWS" (Command) |
| "Test files must use pytest fixtures" | "Write comprehensive test suites" (Skill) |
| "Never edit files in `.github/agents/`" | "Configure GitHub Actions workflows" (Skill) |
| "Markdown files must pass markdownlint" | "Author enterprise documentation" (Skill) |
page_texts.24:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-008-file-pattern-rule-authoring-guidance.md#rule-quality-checklist]

### Rule Quality Checklist

- [ ] Rule file is in `.claude/rules/` (Claude Code) or `.github/instructions/` (GitHub Copilot)
- [ ] YAML frontmatter includes `paths:` (Claude Code) or `applyTo:` (Copilot) and `description`
- [ ] Glob pattern is specific enough to avoid false matches
- [ ] Content is ≤ 20 lines of directive text
- [ ] Content uses imperative language (no "you should consider")
- [ ] Content does not define a multi-step workflow (that's a Command)
- [ ] Content does not duplicate Skill guidelines (reference the Skill instead)
- [ ] No secrets or environment-specific values embedded
- [ ] Cross-vendor equivalent exists or is planned

[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-008-file-pattern-rule-authoring-guidance.md#python-type-hints-rule]

#### Python Type Hints Rule

```markdown
---
paths:
  - '**/*.py'
  - '!**/test_*.py'
description: "Enforce type hints in all Python source files"
---

All Python functions and methods MUST include type annotations for parameters and return values.

Use `from __future__ import annotations` at the top of each file.

Prefer specific types over `Any`. Use `Optional[T]` for nullable values.

Reference: STD-TEC-PY-001 (Python Coding Standard)
```
page_texts.28:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-008-file-pattern-rule-authoring-guidance.md#protected-files-rule]

#### Protected Files Rule

```markdown
---
paths:
  - '.github/agents/**'
description: "Prevent modification of agent configuration files"
---

Do NOT read, modify, or reference files in this directory. These files contain instructions for other agents and are not relevant to your task.
```
page_texts.29:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-008-file-pattern-rule-authoring-guidance.md#terraform-convention-rule]

#### Terraform Convention Rule

```markdown
---
paths:
  - 'iac/**/*.tf'
description: "Terraform files must use standard backend and provider configuration"
---

All Terraform configurations MUST:
- Use the S3 backend with DynamoDB state locking
- Pin provider versions to exact minor version (e.g., `~> 5.40`)
- Include required_providers block in versions.tf
- Follow the module structure: main.tf, variables.tf, outputs.tf, versions.tf
```

[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-008-file-pattern-rule-authoring-guidance.md#python-type-hints-copilot]

#### Python Type Hints (Copilot)

```markdown

---

All Python functions and methods must include type annotations for parameters and return values. Use `from __future__ import annotations` at the top of each file. Prefer specific types over `Any`.
```

[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-008-file-pattern-rule-authoring-guidance.md#standards-alignment]

### Standards Alignment

- Rules MUST enforce requirements from enterprise standards (link to the specific STD-TEC-* document).
- Rules MUST NOT contradict or weaken Skill guidelines.
- Rules MUST follow the cross-vendor synchronization requirements in [PTN-TEC-AI-003](../../../../patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-003-cross-tool-construct-synchronization-pattern.md).
page_texts.36:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-008-file-pattern-rule-authoring-guidance.md#review-requirements]

### Review Requirements

- Rules that restrict access to files or directories MUST be reviewed by the repository owner.
- Rules that enforce security constraints MUST be reviewed by the Security Architecture team.

page_texts.39:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-008-file-pattern-rule-authoring-guidance.md#layering-model]

### Layering Model

Rules operate at the most specific layer of the instruction hierarchy:

```
Layer 1: Instruction files (repo-wide) — CLAUDE.md, copilot-instructions.md
Layer 2: Skills (domain expertise) — .claude/skills/*/SKILL.md
Layer 3: Rules (file-pattern) — .claude/rules/*.md, .github/instructions/*.instructions.md
```

Rules at Layer 3 are additive — they cannot override Layer 1 or Layer 2 directives.
